coverage_policy: This is a partial semantic decomposition. Every supplied Markdown source unit is also indexed. Model theorem links never close implementation or empirical obligations.

claims.claim: Qualified external attackers preserve validator liveness and resource bounds with the host firewall disabled.
claims.model_scope: Only the conditions necessary to claim qualification, not validator liveness.

claims.claim: Return reachability and public identifiers do not establish authorization.
claims.model_scope: Verified identity and payload authentication are abstract inputs; cryptographic correctness is not proved.

claims.claim: Every unvalidated attempt reaching Retry policy is challenged before full handshake acceptance.
claims.model_scope: Pure pre-accept decision; packet parsing, token validation and all role/swarm wiring remain open.

claims.claim: Retry retains nonzero aggregate work and unvalidated traffic cannot consume privileged source quota.
claims.model_scope: Accounting units and provenance rule only; actual packet costs and accounting keys remain open.

claims.claim: Queue, pending and established limits compose across both swarms and diverse attacker identities.
claims.model_scope: Weighted resource composition, pending-pool traces and a discrete handshake cost envelope are proved. Runtime cost dominance, real counter caps, all swarms and omitted allocations remain open. The source-admission count also has a weighted discrete rate envelope; pre-budget rejection work and other resource classes require separate cost bounds. Receipt-gated policy/source traces preserve the accepted-start rate and cost envelopes across policy changes; module 42 adds a shared policy-work budget that charges processed attempts and publications even when denied, and composes its symbolic cost envelope with accepted-start work. Guard, receipt-production, maintenance, completion and established-resource costs remain open. Fueled ingress polls additionally bound all dispatched-event overhead by fuel times an assumed eventCost and compose it with the selected prefix policy/handshake envelopes. Concrete dispatch costs, pre-dispatch work and executor costs remain open. Persistent FIFO service rounds now share a single policy/handshake cost envelope over their actual dispatched trace, with each initial burst counted once across all turns. Arrival processing, queue storage and empty-turn costs remain outside the dispatch envelope. Finite varying-fuel schedules now compose the same envelope over the actual dispatched trace, using total delivered fuel for dispatch allowance and counting each initial burst once. Concrete costs and work outside dispatch remain open.

claims.claim: Closed admission, peer management and optional early refusal share one versioned admission contract.
claims.model_scope: Whole-view generations, stale callback rejection, coherent captured readers and generation/epoch/identity-bound receipts are proved in the model. Runtime linearization through decision use, authoritative input validation, external governance ordering and cryptographic binding remain open. Current policy receipts now gate the atomic source/global/pending transition. Rejected receipts cannot alter resource state or emit an admission receipt; fresh allowed query results delegate to the source transition.

claims.claim: Missing, stale or contradictory policy relaxes authorization without disabling authentication or resource isolation.
claims.model_scope: Modeled missing, stale and contradictory inputs select Grace without removing authentication. Mixed policy/source traces preserve shared handshake credit, per-resident source quota, source-table size and pending occupancy bounds during policy changes; publication preserves the entire source-admission state. Real fault detection, atomic publication, complete accounting and service isolation remain open. Module 42 gates attempts and publications with an independent work budget, including Open/Grace and denied operations, while preserving cleanup and trusted clock progress. Runtime work ordering, costs and policy-recovery scheduling remain open.

claims.claim: Recovery requires valid inputs and enough current-committee records, separate from connectivity and readiness.
claims.model_scope: Versioned recovery clears evidence on replacement or invalidation and rejects unverified, epoch-mismatched and duplicate updates. Verified unresolved members have an enabled update. Signature binding, real member indexing, timestamps, external snapshot ordering and the positive committee-minus-f threshold remain open.

claims.claim: Admission, retention and load-penalty exemptions are distinct; violations still permit bans and trust never removes budgets.
claims.model_scope: Penalty and budget decisions only; retention and actual peer lifecycle remain open.

claims.claim: Legitimate bulk service cannot starve votes, certificates or epoch records.
claims.model_scope: A FIFO rank model proves completion after enough service rounds, despite later bulk arrivals. Real queue projection, scheduler fairness and wall-clock latency remain open.

claims.claim: All Accept, Retry, Refuse and Ignore paths have bounded poll work and preserve task progress and wakeups.
claims.model_scope: Finite polls have bounded work and preserve retained backlog with a wakeup request. Real waker registration, executor fairness, infinite arrival handling and runtime timing remain open. Policy-ingress polls now meter every dispatched event, preserve the exact ordered continuation, and request wake only for retained backlog. Prefix execution and resumption preserve ingress state semantics; positive fuel and actual executor service remain assumptions. Persistent FIFO queue states now append finite arrivals behind retained work and carry the resource state across polls. Repeated unit-fuel rounds execute exactly their dispatched trace and dispatch at most one event per turn. A fixed queued prefix completes after its length of delivered service rounds despite intervening arrivals; real wakers, queue bounds and wall-clock progress remain open. Finite varying-fuel schedules, including zero-fuel turns, preserve exact state and FIFO queue reconstruction. An original prefix is dispatched whenever total delivered fuel equals its length plus natural slack; the resulting resource state executes that prefix before subsequent dispatched work. Real fuel delivery, wakers, queue bounds and wall-clock progress remain open.

claims.claim: Metrics have correct stages and bounded labels, tables, retention and logging; runs record current provenance.
claims.model_scope: Finite metric label domain and fixed-capacity source-table churn are modeled. Runtime exporters, per-entry allocation costs and bounded retention time remain open.

claims.claim: Resolved dependencies, advisories, carried patches and KeyLogFile behavior are explicitly maintained.
claims.model_scope: Dependency and maintenance evidence is operational, not a mathematical consequence of the model.

claims.claim: Always-on Retry applies to every role and swarm while preserving stock-dialer interoperability and bounded incoming queues.
claims.model_scope: Local decision and symbolic slot capacity only; no wire interoperability proof.

claims.claim: Node-side progress survives the Retry fork and effective inbound/outbound deadlines are controlled and measured.
claims.model_scope: Abstract poll budget and minimum deadline, not actual timer propagation or separate dial/accept settings.

claims.claim: Pending lifecycle, validated attribution, handshake-start rate and established limits each have independent bounded accounting.
claims.model_scope: Generation-tagged pending ownership and shared token-bucket bounds compose with policy changes. Keyed source-system traces compose churn and restrictions. Atomic source-admission attempts now jointly gate validated source quota, shared credit and a selected pending slot, preserving the entire state on refusal. Mixed admission, maintenance, clock and completion traces retain source-table width, pending capacity, bounded credits and per-resident debt. Internal receipts carry slot indices and generations; completion preserves source debt and global credits. For arbitrary pending prefixes and suffixes, eligible admission charges and reserves only the selected slot, emits its exact receipt and counts one start. Matching completion releases once; mismatched and stale callbacks preserve the newer owner, and duplicate matching completions advance the generation only once. Held or out-of-range selection preserves state and emits no receipt. Accepted-start conservation now follows actual admission receipts and full updated states, yielding a coupled discrete burst-plus-rate envelope for arbitrary source and pending indices. Current policy receipts now gate the same pre-state admission and exact indexed receipt. Arbitrary policy/source traces retain the state and receipt-counted rate bounds through source-trace erasure. Wall-clock rate bounds, per-source live pending attribution, established resources, runtime policy/source linearization, ConnectionId refinement, machine wrap, runtime unique keys and atomic enforcement, verified expiry, restarts, cap changes and honest reconnect fairness remain open. Fueled policy-ingress polls preserve pending capacity and exact continuation execution. Completion and maintenance bypass exhausted policy work credit when poll fuel remains; cleanup priority and bounded latency remain open. Persistent FIFO ingress service now reaches any queued target, including completion and maintenance, after its preceding prefix length plus one delivered unit-fuel turns, despite finite arrivals on every turn. The resulting pending state retains its original capacity bound; runtime service, receipt validity, queue growth, established resources and wall-clock cleanup latency remain open. Finite varying-fuel schedules retain the pending-capacity bound and exact dispatched-state semantics. Enough cumulative delivered fuel services an original prefix, including queued completion or maintenance, while later dispatched events may further change state. Runtime delivery, trusted receipt refinement, established resources and per-source pending attribution remain open.

claims.claim: Crypto, certificate-work, early refusal and transport restructuring remain separately justified and preserve authentication and compatibility.
claims.model_scope: Cryptographic verification and optimization equivalence require additional formal models and profiling.

claims.claim: A1-A12 provide authoritative admission, trusted redial, seeded startup, record checks, closed-mode behavior and observer connectivity.
claims.model_scope: Only pure admission decisions; each of the listed lifecycle mechanisms needs decomposition and proof.

claims.claim: Hub, Rotation and Later work preserves bounded source accounting, eviction, record freshness, re-resolution and reload semantics.
claims.model_scope: Finite source churn preserves existing debt, bans and simultaneous restrictions; trusted expiry removes debt or bans independently. Keyed source-system and source-admission traces exercise protected churn, claimed-expiry refusal, and registration followed by admission. Source maintenance preserves shared credits and pending ownership; completion preserves source restrictions, and debt expiry does not refill credit. Fixed-quota state bounds are under H16 (C06, C08, C11, C14). Runtime refinement, policy and cumulative-rate integration, verified timers and retention, restart persistence, real admission enforcement and the remaining A13-A27 Hub, Rotation and Later obligations remain open.

claims.claim: Serve paths avoid sleeping under permits and enforce Vote admission, bounded task creation, per-class work and hold-time bounds.
claims.model_scope: The phase/permit policy and a FIFO critical-service progress bound are proved in the model. Rust task transitions, queue projection, hold times and executor scheduling remain open.

claims.claim: Hub serve work remains bounded and aggregate-verification changes require established proof of possession.
claims.model_scope: S7-S9 are open; no proof-of-possession assumption is silently inserted.

claims.claim: Gossip verification work and publishing are bounded, and role-aware scoring does not replace budgets or ban needed honest hubs under load.
claims.model_scope: A full-queue refusal decision and load-penalty rule only. No proof of real nonblocking publish, propagation or library limit ordering.

claims.claim: Live-pack and persistence latency meet an agreed criterion; failed measurements trigger required storage changes.
claims.model_scope: Empirical persistence claims and conditional interventions remain open.

claims.claim: The submit front screens methods, rejects batches, authenticates source attribution and distinguishes refusal/overload from transaction verdicts.
claims.model_scope: Parsed request and trusted-proxy flags only; JSON parsing, HTTP status codes, front configuration and binds remain open.

claims.claim: 429/503 and Retry-After handling avoid cascading endpoint demotions.
claims.model_scope: Demotion counter transitions only. Backoff, Retry-After parsing and retry scheduling remain open.

claims.claim: Old submission paths remain until record/URL convergence and new-path tests pass; isolation follows migration.
claims.model_scope: Retirement gate only; actual dissemination, convergence and origin isolation are not proved.

claims.claim: O1-O9 provide bounded operational metrics, logging, quorum/commit signals and private health/metrics binding.
claims.model_scope: Metric label domain only; all operational signals and private binds need implementation checks.

claims.claim: Provider and host networking preserve source addresses and required ports, avoid unsafe consensus rate limits, and meet capacity/diversity requirements.
claims.model_scope: Physical networking, generated rules and provider capacity require configuration analysis and deployment evidence.

claims.claim: Firewall projections permit all protocol peers and may pre-permit future validators without granting protocol admission.
claims.model_scope: Per-identity set inclusion only; addresses, ports, generated rule ordering and governance provenance need refinement.

claims.claim: Hub key custody, removal, replacement and manual re-key procedures support launch and later reload/rotation.
claims.model_scope: Operational procedures and rotation-state invariants remain open.

claims.claim: M1-M6 qualify flood resilience, reconnects, topology, resource calibration, shared-source behavior and handshake costs.
claims.model_scope: Missing-evidence blocking policy only; none of the measurement results is fabricated.

claims.claim: Independent fixes and feature release do not imply completed deployment qualification.
claims.model_scope: Conjunction of release evidence; engineering milestones require actual receipts.

claims.claim: Staged closure, rollback and endpoint migration preserve budgets, connectivity and operational liveness.
claims.model_scope: Only budget independence and migration gate. Mixed-version and rollout liveness remain open.

claims.claim: The resilience claim states the qualified envelope, provider limits and residual real-address/compromised-hub risks.
claims.model_scope: Necessary limits only; external threat assumptions and the actual envelope require approval and measurements.
